correctness.rationale: Every affine maximum configuration projects bijectively to the horizontal board and hence is a unique graph of an additive homomorphism plus one constant. The 13 direction families reduce to exactly twelve unit tests. The 12-line finite-field arrangement gives five quadruple, four triple and twelve double points, preserved in characteristics at least 7; the explicit p=2,3,5 exceptions and zero p=7 boundary complete the prime count. Unit lifting and Chinese remainder counting establish the formula for every modulus. A packaged Python checker independently tests all slopes and queen-line conflicts at small moduli and confirms the rational incidence certificate; computations are corroborative only.

value.rationale: The affine maximum family is canonical under the maximality/vertical-projection constraint, not an arbitrary slice. The theorem completely enumerates an infinite geometrically natural subclass in a recently highlighted open counting problem and exposes precise arithmetic dependence on prime factors and offsets. Existence alone cannot give these multiplicities; the exact subclass count supplies structured lower bounds for total maximum placements.
